problems: E05 classifies the cCRE as inactive in MCF-7, even though E25-E27 and the family-screen rows report TF occupancy there. Occupancy alone does not demonstrate that the cCRE is functional or mediates regulation in this context.

TOX3 is a strong genetic candidate (E08), but the reported cCRE contact is from other biosamples (E06), and there is no element perturbation or linked eQTL. E09's GTEx-negative result does not rule out a context-specific effect in MCF-7.

E07 lists T as the effect allele in multiple breast-cancer associations but also includes a breast-cancer association with C as the effect allele. The direction of any molecular effect on TOX3 is not established, so the binding predictions cannot be translated into a disease mechanism; this is especially unresolved for H5, which predicts greater binding to C.

critique.next_experiment: Test the element's function in a relevant breast-cancer context with allele-resolved perturbation: introduce or compare the C and T alleles in an isogenic model, perturb EH38E3180851, and measure TOX3 expression together with allele-specific occupancy for FOXA1, ESR1, and GATA3. The MCF-7 inactivity result makes verifying element activity essential before interpreting TF occupancy as regulatory.

games.reason: Both chains share the same element, gene, and phenotype evidence. The TF-specific evidence favors GATA3: its family model predicts greater binding to T and all six GATA models pass the gate (E14), and GATA3 has MCF-7 ChIP-seq peaks containing the variant, with the nearest summit 8 bp away (E25). MSX2 is also expressed and has a reported summit 19 bp away, but its family models disagree on binding direction (E13); no MSX2-specific ChIP result is separately reported. Thus the GATA3 chain is more directly supported, though neither chain establishes allele-specific occupancy or a causal expression effect.

The shared element, target-gene, and phenotype evidence does not distinguish the chains. A is better supported at the TF-specific links: the GATA-family models consistently predict greater binding to T, and GATA3 is highly expressed in MCF-7 with ChIP-seq peaks at the variant, including a summit 8 bp away. B has a closer-than-nearby MSX2 summit at 19 bp, but its homeodomain models disagree on binding direction. Both TFs have evidence of occupancy, but A has the more directly coherent allelic-binding evidence.
